artworks.title: Cadmus and Harmonia
artworks.description: De Morgan's Pre-Raphaelite pair — the Theban founders already half serpents, Ovid's Illyrian end as quiet metamorphosis.

artworks.title: Cadmus and Harmonia Transformed into Serpents
artworks.description: De Passe's engraving — Cadmus and Harmonia becoming crested snakes after Thebes' disasters gather.

artworks.title: Cadmus and Harmonia (Cadmus cum Uxore in Serpentem)
artworks.description: Solis' Metamorphoses woodcut — the prayer answered as husband and wife take serpent form together.

artworks.title: Cadmus and Harmonia Transformed into Serpents
artworks.description: Maiolica dish — the Theban founders' serpent end for a Renaissance table, Ovid glazed in colour.

popCulture.title: Metamorphoses
popCulture.creator: Ovid
popCulture.description: Ovid's close of the Theban books — Cadmus praying to become a serpent, Harmonia joining him — fixes the founders' end as metamorphosis, not mere exile.

popCulture.title: Cadmus
popCulture.description: The Phoenician founder who sowed dragon's teeth and later left Thebes for Illyria — Harmonia's consort until both wear crested scales.
